children: Slovakia posted a trade deficit of EUR 0.8 million in July 2026, shifting from a surplus of EUR 216.5 million in the corresponding month of the previous year and missing market expectations of a EUR 96.2 million surplus.
This marked the first deficit since January, as imports outpaced exports.
Year-on-year, imports climbed 9.4% to EUR 9,062.8 million, mainly due to higher purchases of machinery and transport equipment, which increased by nearly 11%.
Imports from the EU rose almost 13%, while those from non-EU countries increased by approximately 4%.
Meanwhile, exports rose 6.6% to EUR 9,062.0 million, driven largely by a more than 6% increase in shipments of machinery and transport equipment.
Additionally, exports to the EU grew nearly 7%, while those to non-EU countries increased almost 7%.
Over the January–July 2026 period, the country’s trade surplus widened to EUR 1,655.1 million from EUR 1,458.4 million in the same period of 2025.

title: Slovakia Trade Balance Shifts to Deficit in July
